messages.author: ab44118d45997bae
messages.subject: Values used in calculate()
parts:
Hi there,

I'm using nimbe for the first time after using JAGS and coding my own MCMCs. This is such a great middle ground between those two approaches! I'm loving the package and am impressed by the speed! 

I'm trying to conduct some posterior predictive checks on a removal model (abundance model) I fit using nimble. The data model is:
 
y[j,t,i] ~ dbin(N[j,t,i], p[j,t,i]) 

where y[j,t,i] is the number of animals removed in hunt season j, year t, in site i. N is abundance and p is detection probability, indexed the same. I model p as a function of survey effort and N as a function of landscape and temporal covariates. I don't think the rest of the model structure is relevant here though.

I'm trying to calculate a posterior predictive p-value using deviance (-2* log likelihood) for the data (y) and predicted data points (y.pred). I was able to simulate y.pred using an example posterior prediction nimbleFunction I found in the documentation. I would like to calculate deviance using nimble, and I believe I want nimbleModel$calculate(), but I am am confused about what values this function uses to calculate log probability. I would like to calculate the log probability of both the data and the predictions for each MCMC sample of N and p. I tried a sample (first data point only) using base R and it's incredibly slow (hence wanting to use nimble), but this is what I'm trying to do: 

samples <- (MCMC samples obtained via nimble)
ppSamples <- (poseterior predictive samples obtained through simulation)

ind <- numeric(niter)
for(i in 1:niter/2){ #[j,t,i]
#deviance of predictions
  dev.pred <- -2*sum(dbinom(ppSamples[,"y[1, 1, 1]"],
                         samples[i,"N[1, 1, 1]"],
                         samples[i,"p[1, 1, 1]"],log=T))
#deviance of data
  dev.y <- -2*sum(dbinom(noREdat$y[1,1,1],
              samples[i,"N[1, 1, 1]"],
              samples[i,"p[1, 1, 1]"],log=T))
  ind[i] <- dev.pred > dev.y
}
p.val <- mean(ind)

I hope I provided adequate background to address my question, but if not please let me know.

Thanks again,
Abbey

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Values used in calculate()
parts:
hi Abbey,

You should just be able to add `model$calculate` (to calculate log probability values and/or update deterministic nodes) and/or `model$getLogProb` (to fetch already calculated values) to your posterior prediction nimbleFunction. The key thing is to make sure that you correctly update the values in the model so that you are getting logProb values for 'y' and 'y.pred' based on correctly-updated parent nodes, e.g., something like:

deps <- getDependencies(c('p','N'), self = FALSE)  # this would be in setup code

model$calculate(deps)    # these lines would be in run code
model$getLogProb(c('y','y.pred'))

-chris
